figures.before: What a BIM Model Contains and Who Builds It
figures.alt: Commercial interior rough-in with coordinated HVAC ductwork, sprinkler mains, conduit racks, cable tray, piping, and support systems before drywall
figures.caption: A useful model brings the building systems into a shared spatial conversation. The purpose is not a polished image; it is coordinated information that can guide design, fabrication, field installation, and decisions.

figures.alt: Commercial restroom under construction with accessible clearances, wall backing, plumbing rough-ins, and metal-stud framing
figures.caption: Clash detection is valuable when it converts competing spatial demands into a resolved sequence of decisions before the trades commit the work above the ceiling.

figures.before: BIM Execution Plan: What to Include in the Contract
figures.alt: Construction planning table with drawings, measuring tools, a blank clipboard, and coordination materials
figures.caption: The execution plan needs to make the practical rules clear: participants, model uses, information level, deadlines, coordination meetings, clash process, authority to decide, deliverables, and the connection to field work.
